newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen-Further dlr rise would cause problems.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen-Further dlr rise would cause problems.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Monday that a further rise in the dollar exchange rate against the mark would cause price problems in the long term.

Jochimsen, who was speaking at a news conference, also said that normalisation of the mark against the dollar seen in the course of last year did not harbour a danger of inflation and instead was benefiting Germany's export economy.
He added that he would be disturbed if the dollar "shot through the roof like it did against another bid currency".
Jochimsen was referring to the Japanese yen.
Asked if the weakening of the dollar versus the mark in recent days represented a threat to german exporters, Jochimsen said: "To the extent about which we are talking, not at all."
The dollar, which rose to a high of 1.7389 against the mark in late April, has dropped back sharply in the last few trading sessions and was quoted at 1.6907 marks by 1029 GMT.
Jochimsen also said that an overshoot of a currency in any direction was a "very bad thing".
The Bundesbank council member added: "There is no question that if the dollar rate rises further in the long term, that would cause a problem."

Asked whether the mark's depreciation against the dollar over the last year was causing inflationary pressure, Jochimsen said: "I think the normalisation of the mark in the course of the last year could not be dangerous.
"Overall, the competitive element has been very effective in strengthening the position of exporters," he said.
